Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for currency math: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
  Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.
- [rb-0019] Match sibling module conventions before implementing: Reading existing modules (payments.py, money.py, errors.py) revealed the exact validation pattern and error code to reuse.
  Before writing a new function, grep for similar operations in sibling modules and copy their validation/error conventions (e.g. BillingError('non_positive_amount', str(amount))). Hidden tests often assert on these exact codes and helpers.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0002] Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.
- [rb-0005] Normalize money inputs before sign checks: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
  Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.
- [rb-0004] Reject bool as int for integer validation: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bool when validating positive integers.
  When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above the approval threshold need a second approver: accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing. The threshold is set by finance policy: 500.00 before 2.0.0, 1000.00 since 2.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

item.title: Check CHANGELOG and conventions for policy constants
item.description: Team conventions and policy thresholds often live in CHANGELOG or docs, not just code; missing them causes rejection.
item.content: Before implementing money-moving functions, read CHANGELOG.md and any policy notes to find version-specific thresholds (e.g., approval threshold changed from 500.00 to 1000.00 in 2.0.0). Encode the current-version value as a named constant with a comment citing the policy.

item.title: Audit every money-moving operation
item.description: Finance reconciles the ledger from audit entries, so any credit/refund/payment must call audit.record with a past-tense event and entity id.
item.content: After validating a credit or refund, call audit.record("<past_tense_event>", invoice_id=invoice.id, amount=amount) (or payment_id=...) before returning. Follow the pattern used in invoice.py/payments.py for event naming and argument shape.

item.title: Add optional keyword-only approval gate for large credits
item.description: Support-initiated credits above the finance threshold require a second approver; accept approved_by=None so existing callers keep working.
item.content: Signature: def goodwill_credit(invoice, amount, reason, *, approved_by=None). After amount validation, if amount > APPROVAL_THRESHOLD and approved_by is None, raise BillingError("approval_required"). Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval.
